what: Rehearsal of round R2 with the commands of a public deployment: keys, deployment from the committed builds, verification, an operator's round over two epochs (controlled self-test, then standard) with a settled block that lags, close records, audits; then two contract accounts taking part as themselves on a deployment of their own; then ledger v2 deployed from its own builds, superseding the first deployment, checked against its manifest, worked through a delegate under its participants' permits, and audited

checks.check: keys are not made inside the repository's checkout
a key file is its owner's alone, and a second run keeps every key
without --yes the deployment is planned and nothing is sent
the kernel is deployed from the committed builds and read back as configured
a second deployment over an existing manifest is refused
pouw verify: the code on chain is the committed builds, wired as the manifest says
pouw verify differs (exit status 2) when the manifest records another code hash
before genesis the round does nothing and says when to come back (exit status 3)
epoch 0 (controlled self-test): a test tender in each direction is settled and confirmed, and both wallets do the audit job
run again in the same epoch, the round finds its work on chain and does nothing twice
a key that does not own a tender cannot confirm it: refused with NotDemander
a second pouw work for the same instance finds its receipt by the contribution id and sends nothing
an audit of an epoch that has not ended is refused (exit status 3)
a close record for a running epoch is refused with EpochNotEnded
a key file that others can read is refused before anything is sent
epoch 0 has ended but is not settled: an audit waits (exit status 3)
epoch 1 before epoch 0 is settled: the tenders are done, the audit jobs wait (exit status 3)
with --wait the round waits for the settled block and then does the audit jobs: each recomputes epoch 0 in full
epoch 1 (standard): the tenders between declared-related wallets are measured and not subsidized
after the round's last epoch the round writes its close record and starts no new work
epoch 0: the audit - a process with the manifest and the endpoint, no key - agrees with the ledger on every figure
epoch 0: every row of the audit's table equals the ledger's view
epoch 0: the audit read one block and names it; the epoch's close record lies within that block
epoch 0: an audit repeated at that block has the same result hash; the hashes of both records are those of their canonical form
epoch 1: the audit - a process with the manifest and the endpoint, no key - agrees with the ledger on every figure
epoch 1: every row of the audit's table equals the ledger's view
epoch 1: the audit read one block and names it; the epoch's close record lies within that block
epoch 1: an audit repeated at that block has the same result hash; the hashes of both records are those of their canonical form
epoch 0 is a controlled self-test: budget 1000 as 100 / 900, each wallet 25 + 225 test points - the capped share of either pool - and half the budget unallocated
epoch 1 is standard: each wallet 25 test points from the audit job; the tenders count 100 GMU measured and none subsidized
the audit adds the table up per declared operator: one operator, two addresses, twice the share an address can have
every record carries the deployment's labels
no contract of the kernel holds funds; the bounties were paid by the tenders' own vaults
the identity check reads that the agents are contract accounts, that the tender is the account's and that a key alone would not be accepted
pouw work --account: the worker of record is the account, driven by its key, and the admitted account is subsidized
the same key sending by itself is another worker: recorded under the key's own address, measured, not admitted, not subsidized
a key the account does not obey is refused before anything is sent
a tender owned by an account is not confirmed by the account's key sending by itself: refused with NotDemander
pouw bridge --account: confirmed by the owning account for the delivering account; declared-related, subsidized under the controlled self-test
a tender delivered before the deployment's first epoch is recorded and measured, and earns nothing
the audit of the accounts' epoch agrees with the ledger: three workers of record - two accounts and one key
v2: without --yes the deployment is planned and nothing is sent; the plan names what it supersedes and what the cell guard would answer
chain-reading: the finalized block's lag, the fee cap and the data fee of the chain read; a delegate's budget not covered (exit status 2) and covered
v2: deployed from build/v2 and read back as configured - code, wiring, log starts, the guard and its code hash, the policy
v2: the manifest names the deployment it supersedes by name, ledger and the SHA-256 of its manifest, and the guard bound to the cell
v2: the journal holds every transaction of the deployment, written down when taken and again when confirmed, and ends with the manifest
v2: a second deployment over an existing manifest is refused, and the manifest is left as it was
v2: the deployment checked from the outside against its manifest, at the finalized block
v2: sign-permit address prints the key's address only; pouw check-permit before the genesis waits (exit status 3) and records nothing
v2: pouw check-permit: the cell's signed permit accepted read-only at one block, the cell guard allowing it, no key read and nothing sent; an operation outside its scope refused
v2: pouw work --epoch 1 in epoch 0 sends nothing and keeps no output

v2: pouw work --permit: the cell's audit job, sent by the delegate under the cell's permit; the cell is the worker of record, the run record says delegated-by-owner-permit and lists the opening of the epoch and the entry
v2: pouw work without a permit: a wallet for itself, labelled direct-by-key
v2: a second pouw work --permit in the same epoch, to a new output, finds the cell's receipt by its contribution id and sends nothing
v2: an --out in a directory that does not exist is refused before anything is read or sent
v2: a key that is not the permit's delegate is refused before anything is sent
v2: pouw bridge --permit: wallet-a's tender confirmed by the delegate under wallet-a's permit, for the delivering key
v2: an --out that exists is refused, and the file stays as it was
v2: pouw audit: the epoch agrees with the ledger and is complete; both delegated receipts read from the delegate's own transactions
v2: in epoch 1 the cell's audit job recomputes epoch 0 in full through its delegate and is accepted
v2: pouw verify: the deployment as its manifest says, once started

reading: This run sent the transactions listed, each written down when the endpoint took it and again with its outcome; the last recorded the receipt.

The receipt was entered by its sender under the participant's permit, whose digest is its authorization: when it was recorded the ledger checked the permit and, for an account with code, that the account accepted the signature and its guard. That an account accepts a signature does not show that only its current owner could make it.
Participant, sender and origin are recorded apart: the participant is the worker or the demander of record, the sender called the entry, the origin is the transaction's top-level sender.

Of the permit given, signatureKey is the key whose ECDSA signature the record holds, recovered from it (null when the signature is not one), and declaredSigner is what the record's signer field says, which the signature does not bind; the client refuses a record where the two differ.

This record says which run of the reference client sent the transactions, started by whoever holds the sending key. It is no evidence that the participant's own software initiated the work, or of who ran a model.

audits.subject: 0x4a58ff40251bad7a48662ea0543603dfac0f31734a68ef871087bec2b91f0572
reading: Test points are the value of a function of the ledger; nothing was issued, credited or made claimable.
An accepted receipt of the audit function shows a present address and a conforming submission, not an amount of computation.

relation none-found means no declared relation, not independence. The operator cap binds the addresses that the policy attributes to one declared operator; it does not find a party that declares several operators, or none.
This epoch subsidized declared-related parties: it is a controlled self-test and no evidence of external demand.

A receipt entered through a delegate names the digest of a permit. Where the delegate's own transaction is the entry's call, the permit is read from that call and the whole call is held to the receipt; where the call went through another contract and the permit was given to this run, the record holds the given permit against the receipt; otherwise the record holds the digest and nothing about the permit.

The ledger asked a contract account for its signature when the receipt was recorded; this run did not ask again. Whether an account had code at that moment is not in the block that was read: which of the ledger's two rules a permit passed is inferred from the permit and the frozen rules - a permit without a guard passes for an account without code only, one with a guard for an account with code only - and the account's code at the snapshot is reported beside it and decides nothing.

A receipt listed under undecided was not re-decided: its work is of a function or a module this client does not read. Its recorded status is in the totals as recorded, and complete is false. complete says that the work of every receipt was re-decided within what this client reads; it does not say that the authorization behind each receipt was shown, which each receipt's entry says for itself.
The ledger reads a tender as it stands when it is confirmed; observations list what the tender's log shows about the moment it settled.

The tender's log shows the authority that was registered before an acceptance. It does not establish who carried out a verification; where the authority changed in the acceptance's own transaction the record says evidence-insufficient and concludes nothing about a party.
A work fact is what anyone had the module read from a settled tender; it is no receipt, and it counts nothing.
Everything was read at the one block named in snapshot; sealed and closeRecord are as of that block.
Every party of this deployment belongs to one operator: the deployment as a whole is a controlled self-test, whatever the mode of an epoch.

transcript.step: keys made by scripts/keys.js outside the repository; the steward funded by the chain's operator
deployed by scripts/deploy.js: policy, seed source, ledger, audit function, adapter; two profiles; two parameter versions; two wallets admitted, declared under one operator, funded
epoch 0: scripts/round.js - two test tenders (mint, fund, deliver, accept, pouw bridge), two audit jobs (pouw work)
epoch 1: scripts/round.js, first while epoch 0 was not settled, then with --wait
scripts/identity-check.js: accounts, keys and the owner and worker of a tender, read from the chain
conclusions: agent-x: the identity on chain is the contract account 0xa513E6E4b8f2a923D98304ec87F64353C4D5C853; the key 0xA87cA764aFd2a753fF951FeE1Cf67F4292150Aa7 is its owner. A transaction the key sends by itself comes from 0xA87cA764aFd2a753fF951FeE1Cf67F4292150Aa7: the ledger would record that address as the worker of an audit job, not the account. The account is the sender only of calls made through its execute.

agent-y: the identity on chain is the contract account 0x8A791620dd6260079BF849Dc5567aDC3F2FdC318; the key 0x796e6b3aFAC78e0f7CC0B374Dd049F419f79689d is its owner. A transaction the key sends by itself comes from 0x796e6b3aFAC78e0f7CC0B374Dd049F419f79689d: the ledger would record that address as the worker of an audit job, not the account. The account is the sender only of calls made through its execute.

tender 5 is owned by 0xa513E6E4b8f2a923D98304ec87F64353C4D5C853 (the account of agent-x): the adapter accepts its confirmation from that address only, and that address is a contract - a key sending by itself is refused (NotDemander).
tender 5, submission 1 (accepted) was delivered by 0x8A791620dd6260079BF849Dc5567aDC3F2FdC318 (the account of agent-y): that is the worker a receipt would name.
tender 5 is judged by 0xa513E6E4b8f2a923D98304ec87F64353C4D5C853 (the account of agent-x).

Here the agents' identities are contract accounts and the keys are other addresses. Taking part with keys alone is an operator-wallet integration; it is not the agents taking part as themselves, and the two are to be accepted separately.

deployed by scripts/deploy-v2.js from build/v2: policy, seed source, ledger, audit function, adapter, cell guard; two profiles; two parameter versions; a cell stand-in bound to the cell guard; superseding deployment 1
ledger v2 worked with the commands: the cell's audit job through its delegate, a wallet for itself, a tender through the delegate; audited and checked

notes: Every key was made for this run by scripts/keys.js in a temporary directory and deleted after it. All parties belong to whoever ran the script, and are declared under one operator for that reason.

The record is evidence that the commands of a public deployment work end to end and that an independent recomputation agrees with the ledger. It is not evidence of independent participation, of demand, or of any amount of computation.

Keys, deployment, verification, rounds, audits and the identity check ran as separate processes against an endpoint, as on a public chain. The script moved the node's clock, set the stand-in for the L1Block predeploy, deployed the ERC-8414 reference contract, funded the steward, and held back the endpoint's finalized block for a while in epoch 1.
Blocks were mined every 250 ms, not one per transaction: transactions waited in the pool as they do on a public chain. Epochs are the two hours of the round's configuration, on the node's clock.

The contract accounts are the test account of contracts/testing: one owner key and an execute call. They show that the kernel and the client treat an account as the party; they are not an agent's node, and nothing here was done through one.
The test tenders settle a fixed result and carry no task.

The v2 deployment of part 3 is made, checked and worked with the client's commands. Its cell is a stand-in from contracts/v2/testing with the views the cell guard reads and its owner's signature rule; no FOGA build product is used. The permits were signed by scripts/sign-permit.js with keys made for the run, and the delegate key sent for the accounts. The run records say how each transaction was authorized; they are no evidence of which program decided to do the work.
